query: How can Singapore Airlines improve its overall rating and recommendation rate, especially on flights where passengers do not recommend it (Recommended = no)?

per_column.name: crew_service_quality_issues
per_column.rationale: Extracts crew/staff service failures (rudeness, inattentiveness, inefficiency) from review text as a candidate cause of low ratings and non-recommendation. This is a plausible manipulable treatment whose effect on the outcome is being attributed. Not named in the query.

per_column.name: aircraft_modernization
per_column.rationale: Aircraft age/condition (dated, modern, worn) plausibly affects both perceived crew/product experience and the overall rating. It is surfaced from text, not in the query. However it could also act as a parallel treatment; treated as a common contextual driver here.

per_column.name: price_value_alignment
per_column.rationale: Perceived value-for-money is largely a downstream judgment that sits on the causal path between service/product quality and the overall rating/recommendation. Adjusting for it would block part of the very effect being attributed, so it is a mediator rather than a genuine confounder.

judge.rationale: A clear treatment (crew service quality issues) is surfaced from the review text, satisfying part (a). For part (b), only aircraft_modernization is a candidate confounder and it is genuinely surfaced from data rather than copied from the query, but its status as a common cause of BOTH the crew-service treatment and the outcome is weak/ambiguous (it may act as a separate treatment). The remaining added column, price_value_alignment, is a mediator on the causal path to the outcome and adjusting for it would bias the attribution. Overall the set gestures at causal estimation but provides no strong, unambiguous common-cause confounder, so confounder quality is low.
